text:
maya: quick sync — noticed a discrepancy between Python & TS SDKs for /v1/generate when passing optional params (stop_sequences, temperature, top_p). Python serializes unspecified fields as null, TS omits them. Backend currently treats explicit null as "reset to default" vs omitted as "leave server default" which leads to different outputs. Anyone hit this in integration tests or prod? cc @sam @alex

alex: saw this in logs yesterday. Small example from request traces: Python SDK -> {"temperature": null, "stop": null} whereas TS SDK -> {"prompt": "x"} (no temperature key). Server feature flags mean null becomes 0.0 in some models, so callers get colder generations unexpectedly.

sam: repro locally. cURL example that triggers the mismatch:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"Hello","temperature":null}'
```
Response differs from omitting the field entirely.

sam: quick SDK snippets to show behavior:
Python:
```py
client.generate(model="redwood-1", prompt="Hello", temperature=None)
# ends up sending JSON with "temperature": null
```
TS:
```ts
client.generate({model: 'redwood-1', prompt: 'Hello', temperature: undefined})
// SDK drops the key entirely
```

liz: this bit caused a regression in PR #4321 where a service relied on server defaults. CI flagged it: integration/generation/temperature_spec.js failed with a handful of flakes.

ci-bot: Build 2468 — integration tests failed (generation temperature spec). See https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/2468 for logs.

maya: two possible remediation options: 1) change server to treat null the same as omitted (backwards-compatible but riskier across many endpoints), or 2) normalize SDKs to drop keys with None/undefined unless the user explicitly passed a sentinel for "send null". I lean SDK-normalize to keep server simple.

alex: agree with SDK-normalize. Server already has a lot of special-casing. We should also add an explicit "NullValue" sentinel in SDKs for users who want to force null.

sam: I can open a PR for python-sdk to filter None fields before serializing payloads and add a regression test. Will mirror in TS-sdk after. Plan: add util _strip_none(payload) used by all "prepare_request" helpers.

sam: opened issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/212 and draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/213 with tests and changelog entry.

maya: awesome. @liz can you add a short note in the SDK compatibility section of Console docs and add a line to the Dedicated customer changelog for the upcoming release? Might help reduce support noise.

liz: yep, I'll add a doc patch and a small alert for ops. Also will schedule a 15-min sync later this week to review any more contract edgecases. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — assigning final follow-ups to @sam (PR merge + backport), @liz (docs + changelog). Please ping this thread once merged so we can close the loop.

sam: will do, will also add an integration test that mirrors the production trace to catch regressions.

alex: nit — let's also add a short note in the SDK CHANGELOGs about the new NullValue sentinel behavior so users aren't surprised.

maya: agreed. closing for now; will reopen if more patterns crop up.
